To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total pressure drop of sawdust was increased with increasing of inlet air flow.
the contribution rate to total air pressure drop was continuously increased with increase of the inlet air velocity, but the contribution by air filled porosis was decreased.
The contribution rates of the affecting factors to the pressure drop were different with the increasing of inlet air flow and the moisture content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of contribution rates for air permeability of bulking agent in composting.
the contribution rates of affecting factor on total pressure drop for sawdust used as bulking agent on composting.
the affecting factors and contribution rate for air permeability of sawdust as bulking agent on composting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the particle size(SIZExv) is the most important factor for air permeability of bulking agent.
the particle size(SIZEv) and air filledporosity(AFP*v), which are the main affecting factors for the air permeability, have the significant relations with the total pressure drop.
the inlet air flow(v), particle size(SIZE) and air filledporosity(AFP) had a significant influence on total pressure drop for sawdust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the contribution rates for the total pressure drop of sawdust as bulking agent were affected by inlet air flow, particle size and air filled porosities. And the contribution rates of affecting factor were changed by inlet air flow and moisture content.
the inlet air flow and particle size of the bulking material are important factors to determine the pressure drop in the composting process.

the inlet air flow is the most important factor affecting to the total pressure drops in the sawdust used bulking agent in composting, and the contribution rates to total pressure drop for air filled porosity, moisture content and particle size were 0.3, 0.3 and 0.3 respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to estimate the contribution rates for affecting factors on the total pressure of air permeability for the sawdust as bulking agent on the composting process.
the air permeability of sawdust as a bulking agent in composting is affected by inlet air flow, particle size and moisture content of bulking agent.
we have shown the contribution rates for affecting factors to the total pressure drops in composting process.
